title: Past perfect continuous, past perfect and past continuous
subtitle: I'd been finishing / I'd finished
summary: Choose between the past perfect continuous, the past perfect and the past continuous when looking back from a point in the past.

lesson.heading: In progress or finished before that past moment?

left.label: Past perfect continuous - still in progress
left.text: Something was in progress recently before, or right up to, a past point in time.
examples: I**'d been finishing** some work in the garden when Lea arrived, so I didn't hear her come in. (not ~~I'd finished some work in the garden when Lea arrived~~)

right.label: Past perfect - the activity was over
right.text: The activity was already finished before that past time.
examples: I**'d finished** all the ironing so I started cleaning the windows. (not ~~I'd been finishing all the ironing~~)

lesson.note: Often either works: I'd been working / I'd worked hard all year, so I felt that I deserved a holiday.

lesson.heading: How many times?
lesson.text: If we say how many times something happened in a period up to a particular past time, we use the past perfect, never the past perfect continuous.

examples.text: How many times **had you met** him before yesterday?
examples.wrong: How many times had you been meeting him

examples.text: I **had stayed** in the hotel twice in the 1990s.
examples.wrong: I had been staying in the hotel twice

lesson.heading: Three ways the activity can end
lesson.text: The past perfect continuous describes an activity that went on before a particular past time and then (i) finished at that time, (ii) carried on beyond it, or (iii) finished shortly before it.

examples.text: We**'d been driving** for about an hour when the engine suddenly stopped.
She felt terrible during the interview because she **had been suffering** from flu since the previous day.
When I last saw Omar, he**'d been running** and was out of breath.

left.label: Past perfect continuous - we care how long it went on
examples: When the merger was announced it became apparent that the two companies **had been discussing** the possibility since last year.
I first met Mateo and Lucia when they **had been going** out together for five years, and they didn't get married for another three years after that.

right.label: Past continuous - the length doesn't interest us
examples: A friend told me about a conversation she'd recently overheard. Two women **were discussing** their holiday plans ...
Karin met Lars when she **was going** out with his best friend.

lesson.heading: States stay simple
lesson.text: We don't describe states with continuous tenses, so we use the past perfect - even when we focus on how long the situation lasted up to a particular past time.

examples.text: We **had** only **owned** the car for six weeks when the clutch broke.
examples.wrong: We had been owning the car for six weeks

lesson.heading: Mainly a written form
lesson.text: The past perfect continuous belongs mostly to written texts and is much less common in speech. Newspaper reports use it freely.

examples.text: The body of a climber who went missing in the Alps was finally found yesterday. Carl Sims **had been climbing** alone near the Harz Waterfall, which has claimed many lives in the past.

lesson.text: A number of times, or a state, forces the plain past perfect. Everything else is a choice about whether you want the activity to feel unfinished.

exercises.prompt: The avalanche ___ them 500 metres down the mountain but no one was hurt.
exercises.explanation: A single completed action before the past point, so the past perfect.

exercises.prompt: She took a bottle from the bag she ___ all the way from home.
exercises.explanation: Carrying the bag was an activity going on up to that moment, so the past perfect continuous fits best.

exercises.prompt: This was the first time we had been to the castle, even though we ___ Prague a few times before.
exercises.explanation: A few times gives a number of occasions, so the past perfect continuous is impossible.

exercises.statement: How many times had you been meeting him before yesterday?
exercises.explanation: How many times had you met him before yesterday? How many times calls for the past perfect.

exercises.prompt: She had only ___ for the company for a couple of months, so I was surprised to hear that she'd left.
exercises.explanation: An activity in progress up to that past point takes the past perfect continuous; the past perfect is also possible.

exercises.prompt: Explain why you didn't hear Lea come in.
exercises.answer: I'd been finishing some work in the garden when Lea arrived
exercises.explanation: The work was still in progress, so the past perfect continuous - not I'd finished - is right.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of these sentences.

pairs.left: We'd been driving for about an hour
She felt terrible during the interview
pairs.right: because she had been suffering from flu since the previous day.
he'd been running and was out of breath.

pairs.left: Carl Sims had been climbing alone near the Harz Waterfall,
pairs.right: which has claimed many lives in the past.

pairs.left: We had only owned the car for six weeks

exercises.prompt: She bought her first watch at the age of eight. It ___ two pounds.
exercises.explanation: Cost describes a state here, and states are not used in continuous forms.

exercises.statement: My teacher was really annoyed with me. It was the third time I had arrived late for school that week.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The third time counts occasions, so the past perfect is right.

exercises.prompt: When the plane was diverted, shortly after take-off, it ___ from London to Frankfurt.
exercises.explanation: The flight was in progress at that past moment, so the past perfect continuous.

exercises.statement: We had been owning the car for six weeks when the clutch broke.
exercises.explanation: We had only owned the car for six weeks when the clutch broke. Own describes a state, so no continuous form.

exercises.prompt: Which form does each sentence need?

items.text: Mrs Bishop ___ to have children for years, and only became pregnant at 45. (try)
Even though we ___ Prague a few times before ... (visit)
Emma Willems ___ novels for ten years before she published her first book. (write)
It was the third time I ___ late for school that week. (arrive)
We ___ about Sarah when, to our amazement, she walked through the door. (talk)
